conditions: Rigid body rotating about a fixed axis in classical mechanics; I evaluated about that axis.

symbols.I: Moment of inertia about the rotation axis

spoken_aliases: k equals one half times capital i times omega squared
rotational kinetic energy equals one half times moment of inertia times angular speed squared

evidence: Each mass element of a rigid body rotating about a fixed axis has speed omega times its perpendicular distance r from that axis. Summing its classical kinetic energy gives omega^2/2 times the mass-weighted sum of r^2, which is the moment of inertia.
Reference checked 2026-11-27: https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-1/pages/10-key-equations. Proposed maintainer approval, not independent human certification.
